actor_attribution_analysis.trace: reconcileInstanceEngineDrive claims engineTaskId to args.actor. args.actor is bound at both post-approve call sites (inbox.ts:2607 main approve, inbox.ts:2341 defer/T-0638) from `const actor = await extractActorSlug(req, () => pool)` (inbox.ts:2144). extractActorSlug (inbox.ts:108) resolves the AUTHENTICATED identity: keycloak mode -> resolveActorSlugFromAuth(pool, ctx.sub, ctx.preferredUsername) from the VERIFIED token (401 if no employee matches); dev mode -> x-dev-user header. The request BODY is read only for `action` and `outcome` — there is NO body path that can inject actor/assignee.
actor_attribution_analysis.same_actor_as_authz: The identical `actor` value is used for the approve-grant eligibility check (403 NOT_ELIGIBLE) AND for setTaskAssignee. So the assignee recorded in engine history is exactly the authenticated + authorized actor — a caller cannot mask 'who completed' as someone else beyond what the existing authz already grants. In prod (keycloak) the slug derives from the verified JWT, so it is not caller-controlled. No NEW attack surface introduced by T-0672.

idempotency_analysis.claim_only_on_live_task: The claim block is nested inside `if (engineTaskId)` — it fires ONLY when getActiveUserTasks returned a live active task. Once a task is completed it disappears from the runtime task list, so a second click/re-drive resolves engineTaskId=null, skips the claim entirely, and falls to the isInstanceEnded branch. The recorded assignee is never overwritten.
idempotency_analysis.reconcile_on_read_never_claims: reconcileWaitingInstancesEngineDrive passes completeEngineTask:false (process-projection.ts:2402); the whole completion+claim block is guarded by `if (args.completeEngineTask && ...)` so read-path never claims.
idempotency_analysis.proven_live: The idempotent live test re-drives an already-ended instance with actor='someone-else' and asserts rawHistoricAssignee still == the first actor. PASS. Directly refutes the 'second clicker clobbers the completer' concern.
idempotency_analysis.same_actor_reclaim: Flowable claim with the same assignee is HTTP-200 idempotent (documented + relied on); a re-driven same-actor approve does not fail on the claim step.

non_fatal_analysis.claim_failure: A non-budget claim failure logs a console.warn and PROCEEDS to completeUserTask (process-projection.ts:2105-2113). Unit test 'a claim FAILURE is NON-FATAL' asserts order==[setTaskAssignee, completeUserTask] and a normal 200 (not 502) with exactly one instance.ended. No double-complete: complete is called once regardless of claim outcome.
non_fatal_analysis.budget_exhaustion_on_claim: If the claim call itself exhausts the shared T-0591 deadline it returns ENGINE_DRIVE_TIMEOUT at stage 'complete' (does not fall through to complete). This is EQUIVALENT to pre-fix behaviour under exhaustion: callWithBudget short-circuits every subsequent call once remaining<=0, so complete would have hit BUDGET_EXHAUSTED anyway. The only new effect is one extra in-budget round-trip; worst case is a VISIBLE 502 that the reconcile-on-read net retries and the already-committed human decision is not lost. Consistent with T-0591 fail-visible philosophy — acceptable, non-blocking.

findings.issue: The live suite relies on vitest's DEFAULT 60s per-test timeout, which EQUALS the test's own driveDeadlineMs:60000 — zero headroom for BPMN deploy + poll. findings.suggestion: Set an explicit per-test testTimeout strictly greater than driveDeadlineMs (e.g. testTimeout=90000 with driveDeadlineMs=60000) so a slow deploy+poll cannot blow the vitest budget before the drive budget. Non-blocking robustness nit.
